title: Grade 9 English — The Snake and the Mirror + Reported Speech
description: Beehive Chapter 7 comprehension and Grammar: Reported Speech
subject: english

questions.question: In 'The Snake and the Mirror', the narrator of the story is a:
questions.explanation: The narrator is a young doctor who has just started his practice and rents a room. The story is told in retrospect — he recounts the terrifying experience of a snake landing on his shoulder.

questions.question: What was the doctor doing just before the snake landed on his shoulder?
questions.explanation: The doctor was sitting in front of the mirror, admiring his appearance and daydreaming about marrying a wealthy woman, when the snake fell from the roof and coiled on his shoulder.

questions.question: What did the doctor decide NOT to do when the snake was on his shoulder?
questions.explanation: The doctor remained absolutely still — he decided not to move or shiver because he feared any movement might provoke the snake to bite him. He sat like a statue.

questions.question: What eventually saved the doctor from the snake?
options: The snake noticed its own reflection in the mirror and slid toward it
He threw the snake off his shoulder
questions.explanation: The snake was distracted by its own reflection in the mirror. It uncoiled, slid down the doctor's body, and moved toward the mirror — effectively saving the doctor. The mirror, ironically, saved his life.

questions.question: The 'mirror' in the story symbolises:
questions.explanation: The mirror symbolises vanity — the doctor was admiring himself in it before the crisis, and ironically the snake's vanity (attracted to its own reflection) saved him. The story gently mocks human self-obsession.

questions.question: Change to reported speech: He said, 'I am reading a book.' → He said that he ___
questions.explanation: In reported speech, when the reporting verb is in the past ('said'), the tense of the reported clause shifts back: 'am reading' (present continuous) → 'was reading' (past continuous).

questions.question: Change to reported speech: She said, 'I will go tomorrow.' → She said that she ___
questions.explanation: Tense shift: 'will' → 'would'. Time expression shift: 'tomorrow' → 'the next day' (the following day). Both changes are required in reported speech.

questions.question: Change to reported speech: She asked, 'Are you coming to the party?' → She asked me ___
options: whether I am coming to the party
if I was coming to the party
that I was coming to the party
if I came to the party
questions.explanation: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if' or 'whether' and change to statement word order. Tense: 'are coming' → 'was coming'. ('That' is used for statements, not questions.)

questions.question: Change to reported speech: He said to me, 'Please help me.' → He requested me ___
questions.explanation: Imperatives (requests/commands) in reported speech use infinitive form: 'Help me' (request) → 'requested/asked me to help him'. The word 'please' is dropped; the verb shifts to infinitive.

questions.question: Identify the error in the reported speech: She told that she was hungry.
questions.explanation: 'Tell' requires an object (tell someone), but 'said' does not need a direct object before 'that'. Correct: 'She said that she was hungry.' OR 'She told me that she was hungry.' 'Told that' without an object is incorrect.

questions.question: Change to reported speech: He asked, 'Where do you live?' → He asked me ___
questions.explanation: Wh-questions in reported speech: use the wh-word as conjunction, shift tense, and use statement order (subject + verb). 'Where do you live?' → 'where I lived' (tense shift: do → did, but in reported speech we omit the auxiliary and say 'where I lived').

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses reported speech CORRECTLY?
options: He said he will come tomorrow.
She said that she had finished her work.
They said they are playing cricket.
She told that she is ready.
questions.explanation: 'She said that she had finished her work' is correct: past perfect replaces simple past after a past reporting verb, and 'told' needs an object. Options A and C don't shift tense correctly; D uses 'told' without an object.

questions.question: The story 'The Snake and the Mirror' is written in which narrative style?
questions.explanation: The story is told in first person — the doctor himself narrates the incident to a group of people sitting in darkness during a power cut. 'I' is used throughout, giving it an intimate, confessional feel.

questions.question: The story uses humour and irony. Which of the following is an example of irony?
options: The snake falling from the roof
The doctor admiring himself just before danger arrived
questions.explanation: It is ironic that the doctor was daydreaming about his good looks and a rich wife at the very moment danger (the snake) arrived. The mirror that was a tool of vanity later saved his life — a double irony.

questions.question: Time expression change in reported speech: 'now' changes to:
questions.explanation: Standard time-expression shifts: 'now' → 'then'; 'today' → 'that day'; 'yesterday' → 'the previous day'; 'tomorrow' → 'the next day/the following day'; 'here' → 'there'.

questions.question: The story was written by Vaikom Muhammad Basheer. He was a famous writer in which language?
questions.explanation: Vaikom Muhammad Basheer was a celebrated Malayalam writer known for his humorous, humanistic short stories. 'The Snake and the Mirror' is a translation of his original Malayalam story.
